title: The future of gaming, where ai can take us.
author: crumbaker
selftext:
I've been thinking about this a lot lately. Too much of the discussion has been about replicating the quality of current indie, AA, and AAA games via ai, and not enough about what comes after that. 

We might be there with the Fable 5.2 release. I thought Opus 5.5 was incredible, but the content I've been able to create lately has blown me away. 

So with this level of quality and speed, what can we offer the market that traditional studios can't?

1. Constant episodic content. Weekly or monthly new adventures for your customers.

2. Customization. It's far easier to add features than ever before. There's all sorts of ways a player can make the experience their own that goes well beyond the cosmetics of today.

3. Mega scale. Making another GTA type game? How about instead having a GTA planet. GTA universe? Multi planetary rts's with thousands of players fighting at once etc.

4. In game ai going to the next level by having the dialogue produced by an llm. I can see people getting obsessed in their own sim worlds very soon.

I wanted to elaborate more but I think this post is long enough. Where do you all see ai taking the next era of gaming?

comments.author: RINgames
comments.body: This is what excites me most. Not the same games done faster. Games that could never have been done before.

replies.author: crumbaker
replies.body: We still have performance limitations for sure, and the cost of hardware isn't helping, but beyond that if someone has enough tokens they can make just about anything. What a time to be alive.

comments.author: count023
comments.body:
to me what excites me is that AI can fix up all those "annoyances" in mods. 

Like for instance, a while ago, i played an RE4 mod where they swapped out the lead's character model wtih a different one that was shorter, in cutscenes the camera data and some of the propers were misaligned as a result and clipped or floated in the void or the camera was slightly off. Now the AI can read the scripts for things like pre-rendered cutscenes and fix the animation data so these problems go away. Little QOL things like that. Which is basically a riff on what you're proposing becasue what is an episodic game series except mods/dlcs of extra episodes encoded as scripts/asset bundles on the same shared engine?

comments.author: Upstairs_Tone_4227
comments.body: The issue with 3 and 4 is that while LLMs can produce more volume, that doesn’t mean they can get around current tech limitations to make an optimized game. AI could make some of the stuff you’re describing in a few years but will the average PC be able to run it?

replies.author: crumbaker
replies.body: yeah I mentioned that in another comment, unless the market changes that especially will be an issue with hardware costs. However even on current hardware I think we can exceed the current scale we see. llm dialogue will probably be outsourced to cloud models for the most part.

replies.author: TechgeekOne
replies.body: You definitely can. If there's one pet peeve of mine it's the sheer waste that goes on in modern gaming. I don't even have to try that hard to do better than most code I've seen. If you know anything about memory and how a CPU accesses it then 5-10x speedups are so easy. Eliminating bottlenecks in the data paths and eliminating redundant work is the side of the coin. Though admittedly that's a lot harder in some cases

comments.author: Outside_The_Playtrix
comments.body:
Why would there be a market anymore when everyone can just make their own games? The AI companies have stolen the market- it’s like asking what opportunities we have as horse service providers in this new world of automobiles- 

1. We can collect people and take them to their car.   
2. We can use cars to travel to collect cool things to decorate the horses with that would otherwise be inaccessible.   
3. We could all collaborate to create a horse mega fleet now that our horses aren’t being used for travel purposes and are freed up resources.   
4. Now that people use cars, horses offer a personal touch. Horses have a soul but cars don’t.

replies.author: ChrisDEmbry
replies.body: I take your point, but playing someone else's game is a way to experience someone else's perspective.

replies.author: Outside_The_Playtrix
replies.body:
Yeah there are opportunities to do that, but not enough to make a market for the vast majority of people. For example, in theory, people might still buy GTA games or experiences created by their religious institutions out of brand loyalty. 

5. Rising a horse can still offer people the experience of riding a horse.

replies.author: ChrisDEmbry
replies.body: Since you're still talking about horses, there actually is a very large industry of breeding and racing horses still today.

replies.author: Outside_The_Playtrix
replies.body:
Well firstly that’s a bait and switch, you may have made by accident. It’s not very large at all, compared to the automobile market- so you had to do the mental gymnastics to miss the point, in order to make that point. Secondly, another bait and switch is that this conversation is about games market continuity. Your point would only make sense if you could show that the horse travel market directly evolved into the current horse market, with all the same people staying employed etc.

What I will concede is that the discussion this post is having might lead to some people succeeding in the way that you are describing, but that’s the more honest way to talk about it, rather than talking about it as if the entire market hasn’t just been rendered obsolete. A little thing I like to call living in reality 😅 it’s lonely here though.

replies.author: ChrisDEmbry
replies.body: I see what you're saying, and I'm interested in thinking past this inflection point. I can see games becoming front-ends or wrapper scenarios for AI-driven characters. You pay for the AI service of making the world come alive, and the background of the world (fantasy, cyberpunk, etc.) is free.

replies.author: Outside_The_Playtrix
replies.body: All markets are soon stolen in the same way, so nobody has any money to pay for things anymore. I think that is the inflection point we need to think beyond.

replies.author: ChrisDEmbry
replies.body:
Nobody has money to pay for race horses and steeplechase?

You might not be moving in the right circles to talk about horses, my friend.

comments.author: Serzhe_Nebulife
comments.body: One interesting direction is making large worlds feel coherent as players change them, not just generating more places. In the space game I direct, the shared universe grows from one seed and the server persists player changes; Claude wrote almost all of the code and tests. I’d be interested in how other developers think about keeping generated content and persistent changes understandable to players.

comments.author: West_Satisfaction299
comments.body: I'd say we can offer everything you said not to mention faster bug fixing. I launched my game almost two months ago and users send me messages on social media every now and then with bugs they find. I fix them in the next update which at the moment is an update every 10 days.

comments.author: Agile_Branch_8743
comments.body: Until AI can be creative, I'm mostly excited about it helping accelerate the boring/annoying/mechanical parts of game development (+ a big chunk of testing), and studio management. Things we already used to automate before, just done more efficiently now.

comments.author: teejayaiartdirector
comments.body:
Please don't talk about AAA games as something related to quality games, most AAA games poured millions into can be considered slop that nobody wants to play.

With AI it's so easy to make games that you can have full working prototypes of games in 1 hour, or do disassemble of old games and have 1 full remake of it with porcedural assets within just 1 hour.

AI has made all digital content and games included to have **zero value!** 🔥 

The next big wave within AI gaming will be diffusion gaming where AI makes all the frames on the fly, every game will just be a prompt away! 😍
